([[Shawnee, Kansas]]) | college = [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] (2025–2026) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2026 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2026]]) * [[Jerry West Award]] (2026) * First-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] ([[2025–26 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2026]]) * [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big Ten Freshman of the Year]] (2026) * Big Ten All-Freshman Team (2026) }} '''Keaton Wagler''' (born February 3, 2007) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]]. ==Early life and high school== Wagler was born to Logan and Jennifer Wagler, both of whom played basketball for [[Hutchinson Community College]], known affectionately as "Hutch", in the 1990s.{{cite web |last=Hall |first=Erik |date=February 7, 2026 |title=Keaton Wagler: 5 things to know about the Illinois basketball guard |url=https://www.thetelegraph.com/sports/article/keaton-wagler-facts-illinois-basketball-23-parents-21339547.php |website=The Telegraph |access-date=February 17, 2026}}{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/48037112/keaton-wagler-rise-illinois-freshman |title=The unexpected rise of Keaton Wagler at Illinois |first=Adam |last=Rittenberg |website=ESPN.com |date=February 26, 2026 |access-date=February 26, 2026}} His basketball roots run even deeper. One of his great-grandfathers, one of his grandfathers, an uncle, and his older brother Landon all played at Hutch. The great-grandfather went on to play at [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]] and later ran the [[NJCAA Division I men's basketball championship|national junior-college men's tournament]], and the uncle won a national title while playing for Hutch. Also, his older sister Brooklyn was part of a [[NJCAA Division I Women's Basketball Championship|junior college national championship]] team at [[Kansas City Kansas Community College]] before playing at [[MidAmerica Nazarene Pioneers|MidAmerica Nazarene University]], and Landon also went on to play at MidAmerica Nazarene. Wagler attended [[Shawnee Mission Northwest High School]] in [[Shawnee, Kansas]]. Coming out of high school, he was rated as a four-star recruit. At the time his career high was a 32-point game vs Chaminade (MO) in Quincy, Illinois, which he later shattered scoring 46 points against [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]]{{Cite web |date=2026-01-25 |title=Illinois Freshman Keaton Wagler, Once Overlooked, Drops 46 to Stun No. 4 Purdue |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/illinois-freshman-keaton-wagler-drops-46-to-stun-no-4-purdue |access-date=2026-03-29 |website=SI |language=en-US}}. He received offers from schools such as UT-Rio Grande Valley, LeMoyne, Northern Colorado, Murray State, Oral Roberts, [[UIC Flames men's basketball|UIC]], [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]], [[Southern Illinois Salukis men's basketball|Southern Illinois]], [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]], [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]], Illinois, and Tulsa.{{cite web |last1=Richey |first1=Scott |title=Good Morning, Illini Nation: Offer out to 2025 guard |url=https://www.news-gazette.com/newsletter/content/sports/illini_basketball/good-morning-illini-nation-offer-out-to-2025-guard/article_507deee0-61c9-11ef-aacf-c777b5171ed1.html |website=The News-Gazette |access-date=December 17, 2025}} Ultimately, Wagler committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]].{{cite web |last1=Thomas |first1=Tristan |title=Four-star guard Keaton Wagler commits to Illinois |url=https://www.wcia.com/sports/your-illini-nation/four-star-guard-keaton-wagler-commits-to-illinois/ |website=WCIA.com |access-date=December 17, 2025}} ==College career== In his debut on November 3, 2025, Wagler totaled 18 points, six rebounds, four assists, and two steals in a win versus Jackson State.{{cite web |last1=Richey |first1=Scott |title=Wagler impressing early in his Illini career |url=https://www.news-gazette.com/sports/wagler-impressing-early-in-his-illini-career/article_881288b6-8145-44fb-8176-53ed6ae876e4.html |website=The News-Gazette |access-date=17 December 2025}} On December 6, he recorded 16 points, eight rebounds, and five assists, with zero turnovers in a win over [[2025–26 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]].{{cite web |last1=Lagendorf |first1=Jackson |title=Did Illinois' Keaton Wagler Just Level Up Against Tennessee? |url=https://www.si.com/college/illinois/basketball/keaton-wagler-illinois-level-up-tennessee |work=Illinois Fighting Illini on SI |publisher=SI.com |access-date=16 December 2025}} On December 9, Wagler scored 23 points in a victory against [[2025–26 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]].{{cite web |last1=Reedy |first1=Joe |title=Keaton Wagler's 23 points lead No. 13 Illinois in Big Ten opener |url=https://qctimes.com/sports/college/basketball/article_bc828326-71eb-5fa5-8762-681b4e95d81f.html |website=QuadCityTimes.com |access-date=16 December 2025}} On December 13, he recorded his first career double-double with 19 points and 10 assists in a 83–80 loss to [[2025–26 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]].{{cite web |last1=Richey |first1=Scott |title=Illinois leaning on Keaton Wagler |url=https://www.news-gazette.com/sports/notes-illinois-leaning-on-keaton-wagler/article_0e3f4d29-6b8c-487e-bebc-cb15a1c7e032.html |website=The News-Gazette |access-date=16 December 2025 |date=December 13, 2025}} On January 24, 2026, Wagler recorded 46 points at Purdue, setting a new record for an Illinois freshman in a single game. This also tied [[Andy Kaufmann|Andy Kaufmann’s]] 46 points on December 3, 1990 for the second-most points in a single game for Illinois. Wagler is considered a potential lottery pick in the 2026 NBA draft.{{cite web |last1=Lagendorf |first1=Jackson |title=Four Illini in 2026 NBA Mock Draft – Including a Surprise First-Round Projection |url=https://www.si.com/college/illinois/basketball/illinois-basketball-four-illini-2026-nba-mock-draft-surprise-first-rounder |work=Illinois Fighting Illini on SI |publisher=SI.com |access-date=16 December 2025 |date=December 10, 2025}} The performance represented the most points by a Big Ten basketball player ever scored against an [[AP Poll]] top 5 opponent and the most points ever scored in a road win against a top ten opponent.{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/mbb/article/59257/|title=Illinois and Michigan State Score Men’s Basketball Weekly Honors|accessdate=January 27, 2026|date=January 26, 2026|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]]}} The performance also broke a 58-year old record for points scored by an opponent at [[Mackey Arena]], broke the school single-game record with 9 made three point shots and was the most in a Big Ten road game since [[Mike Woodson]] posted 48 in 1979.{{cite web|url=https://www.pjstar.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2026/01/24/keaton-wagler-illinois-freshman-scoring-records-in-win-vs-purdue/88341042007/|title=Who is Keaton Wagler? Freshman sets records in Illinois basketball victory|author=Huett, Wes|work=[[Peoria Journal Star]]|date=January 24, 2026|accessdate=January 27, 2026}} Following his freshman season, Wagler declared for the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=Keaton Wagler declares for NBA Draft: projection and analysis |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2026/04/12/keaton-wagler-declares-nba-draft-mock-2026-projection-analysis/89492552007/ |website=[[USA Today]] |date=April 12, 2026 |access-date=April 13, 2026 }} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2025–26]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] | 37 || 37 || 33.9 || .445 || .397 || .796 || 5.1 || 4.2 || .9 || .4 || 17.9 {{s-end}} == References == {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://fightingillini.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/keaton-wagler/15216 Illinois Fighting Illini bio] {{2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{Jerry West Award}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Wagler, Keaton}} [[Category:2007 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:All-American college men's basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Kansas]] [[Category:Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball players]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Shawnee, Kansas]]
